title: Book Three · Chapter 34: Four Laps on Saturday
story:
On Monday, Anna takes the little paper from her maths book.

“I'm going to ask,” she says at lunch.

Her friend closes her box and goes with her. Ronan stays at the desk to finish his rice.

When the girls return, Anna has a new sheet. She lays it between her notebook and her bottle.

“Four laps,” she says.

“For the longer run?” Ronan asks.

“Yes. Around the same track.”

“I told the teacher about my three laps,” she adds. “He said I should start at my own speed. We start and finish beside the bench.”

She puts a finger on the little track drawing at the bottom of the sheet. Ronan follows it around the curve.

He looks at her. Three laps were hard last Friday.

“Are you going to do it?”

“I want to try. There are nearly three weeks.”

The run is at eleven on Saturday morning. Anna points to the date on the sheet. She points to the time too.

“We need to be at the field earlier. The teacher will call our names.”

Her friend has chosen a shorter race. It is earlier in the morning.

“Then I can watch Anna,” the girl says.

Anna takes a pencil. She puts her name on the longer run's list. Ronan watches the letters appear.

“Do you want to win?” he asks.

She looks toward the window.

“I want to run all four. I don't want to start too fast and stop on the last lap.”

“Four steady ones.”

“Yes.”

Her friend returns to her desk. Anna puts the sheet in her folder, separate from the house drawings.

“Will you come?” she asks Ronan.

“To watch?”

“Yes. You can stand near our bench.”

“I can come at half past ten.”

Anna smiles. “Good. Bring your loud voice.”

“I usually leave it at home.”

“You bring it to football.”

He laughs. She opens her exercise book as the bell rings.

That evening, Ronan tells Mum about the running day. She is sorting buttons into a small box.

“On Saturday?” she asks.

“Not this one. In nearly three weeks.”

He shows her the date in his notebook. Mum looks at her own work sheet.

“I have a customer that morning. At her home. Ask me again nearer the day.”

Dad is still at work. Ronan leaves the notebook on his own part of the table and helps Mum clear the middle.

Before dinner, he looks at the date again. Below it, he writes eleven for the start. On the next line, he writes half past ten for himself.

He pictures Anna at the last turn. Four laps will bring her past the bench four times.

Ronan closes the notebook. Tomorrow he can ask Kai to come too. On the running day, there can be more than one loud voice beside the track.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

list＝名单；half past ten＝十点半；separate from＝与……分开放；nearer the day＝临近日子时。

## 理解问题

1. Anna自己选的长跑有几圈、什么时候开始？她最想完成什么目标？
2. Ronan答应几点到？Mum那天上午是否完全没有自己的安排？

## 读句子

**Her friend has chosen a shorter race.**

拆开看：Her friend / has chosen / a shorter race.

她的朋友／已经选了／一个距离较短的比赛项目。
